national_raw_news.title: Asian Para Games 2026: India wins 35 medals, including Seven gold
national_raw_news.content: India continued its strong performance at the Asian Para Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan today, as India’s medal tally rose to 35, including nine gold, eleven silver and fifteen bronze. Indians swept all three medals in the men’s discus throw F44/64 event. Devender Kumar clinched gold with a throw of 49.71 m, while Rakesh took silver with 49.35 m. India’s Pranav Soorma won gold in the men’s discus throw F51/52/53 event, scoring 932 points and also setting a new Asian record of 11.66 metres in the F51 event, while Ram Ratan Singh clinched silver with a throw of 10.35 metres, scoring 809 points in the same event. In the Women’s 200m T12 final, Simran clinched gold, clocking 24.80 seconds, setting a new Games record. Tejalben Damor also secured bronze, clocking 25.23 seconds in the same event. Indian para-athlete Deepthi Jeevanji won gold in the women’s 400-metre T20 event, setting a new Games record with a time of 56.36 seconds. In Powerlifting, Ashok won silver in the men’s 65-kilogram category with a lift of 192 kilograms. Shooter Manish Narwal also secured silver in the men’s 10-metre air pistol SH1 event, scoring 233.7 points. Shrishti Arora won bronze in the women’s 10-metre air pistol SH1 event, marking an impressive debut at the Games. In the javelin throw, Pradeep Kumar won silver with a personal best throw of 27.45 metres, while Ayush Verma claimed bronze with a throw of 17.88 metres. Swimmer Himanshu Nandal won bronze in the men’s 400-metre freestyle S11 event, clocking 5 minutes and 10.91 seconds to finish third. India also won five bronze medals in para table tennis today. Jehan Dorab Madan won bronze in the Men’s Singles Class 1 event after losing 3-nil to South Korean Kim Hyeonuk. Baby Sahana Ravi also secured bronze in the women’s singles Class 9 event, while Prachi Pandey secured bronze in the women’s singles Class 6 event. Bhavina Patel secured bronze after facing a 3-nil defeat to China’s Zhang Bian in the Women’s Singles Class 4-5 semi-finals. Sonalben Patel also secured a bronze in the women’s singles Class 3 event after losing her semi-final against South Korea’s Yoon Jiyu in straight games. In Para Archery, India has assured itself of at least five medals, with three Indian pairs reaching their respective finals. The recurve men’s pair of Harvinder Singh and Vijay Sundi, the recurve women’s pair of Bhawna and Pooja, and the compound women’s pair of Sheetal Devi and Payal Nag advanced to their gold medal match. In the individual events, Swati Chaudhary became the first Indian woman W1 archer to reach the final, while Sheetal Devi advanced to the women’s compound final.

national_raw_news.title: Millions of followers pay homage to Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar at Deekshabhoomi on 70th Dhammachakra Pravartan Day
national_raw_news.content: Millions of followers today paid homage to Bharat Ratna Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar at Deekshabhoomi in Nagpur on the occasion of the 70th Dhammachakra Pravartan Day. Addressing the main ceremony, Venerable Wannasiri Mahathero from Myanmar said that Dr. Ambedkar had embraced Buddhism not out of hatred for anyone, but because the Dhamma of the Buddha offered humanity and the world a better society. He said that the responsibility of carrying forward the Dhamma embraced and propagated by Dr. Ambedkar rested with his followers. President of the Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Smarak Samiti, Bhadant Arya Nagarjuna Surai Sasai, along with monks from India and abroad, were present on the dais. Every year, millions of followers visit Deekshabhoomi to pay their respects to Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar, who embraced Buddhism along with millions of his followers at Nagpur on October 14, 1956, on the occasion of Vijayadashami. The day is celebrated as Dhammachakra Pravartan Day since then.The annual observance commemorates the historic conversion of Dr. Ambedkar to Buddhism and his message of equality, liberty, fraternity and human dignity. Extensive arrangements were made by the Nagpur district and muncipal administrations to facilitate the devotees. Adequate security arrangements were put in place by the police. The Central Railway’s Nagpur Division operated additional trains to facilitate the arrival and departure of followers from different parts of the country. Nagpur Metro also operated services from early morning till late at night to ensure convenient travel for the visitors.

national_raw_news.title: PM Modi congratulates Indian medallists after Day 2 of Asian Para Games
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday congratulated Indian para-athletes for their medal-winning performances on Day 2 of the Asian Para Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, praising their determination, perseverance and sporting excellence. In a series of posts on X by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), PM Modi celebrated achievements across para-athletics, para-table tennis, shooting, powerlifting and swimming, highlighting record-breaking performances and successful debuts. Deepthi Jeevanji defended her women’s 400m T20 title with a Games record. PM Modi described her achievement as a demonstration of the “true spirit of a champion”, saying it would inspire young athletes. Simran won gold in the women’s 200m T12 with a record-breaking performance, improving on her silver from the previous edition. Tejalben Damor secured bronze in the same event on her Asian Para Games debut. Nishad Kumar claimed gold in the men’s high jump T47 with a new Games record. Having already won the long jump title, he finished with two gold medals, with Modi praising his versatility and pursuit of excellence. Pranav Soorma won gold in the men’s discus throw F51/52/53 with an Asian record, while Ram Ratan Singh took silver. India also swept the podium in the men’s discus throw F43/F44/F62/F64, with Devender Kumar winning gold, Rakesh silver and Pradeep Kumar bronze with a personal-best throw. In the men’s javelin throw F53/54, Pradeep Kumar secured his second consecutive Asian Para Games silver with a personal best, while debutant Ayush Verma won bronze, also recording a personal best. Other athletics medallists included Preeti Pal, who won silver in the women’s 200m T35; Ravanni Valasanaini, who earned bronze with a personal best in the women’s 1500m T11; Praveen Sharma, who took bronze in the men’s shot put F11; and Hokato Hotozhe Sema, who won bronze in the men’s shot put F56/F57. In para-table tennis, PM Modi congratulated Bhavina Patel for bronze in the women’s singles Class 4-5 and Sonalben Patel for bronze in the women’s singles Class 3, her first individual Asian Para Games medal. Prachi Pandey won bronze on debut in the women’s singles Class 6, becoming the first Indian medallist in that event at the Games. Baby Sahana Ravi secured bronze on debut in the women’s singles Class 9. PM Modi hailed her achievement as a historic breakthrough for India in the standing category. Jehan Dorab Madan added bronze in the men’s singles Class 1. In shooting, Manish Narwal won silver in the men’s 10m air pistol SH1, while debutant Shrishti Arora earned bronze in the women’s event. PM Modi said Arora’s medal marked a promising beginning to her Asian Para Games journey. Ashok secured silver in the men’s under-65kg para-powerlifting competition, drawing praise from the Prime Minister for his perseverance and self-belief. In swimming, Himanshu Nandal won bronze in the men’s 400m freestyle S11, while Niranjan Mukundan claimed bronze in the men’s 200m individual medley SM7. PM Modi extended his best wishes to the medallists for their future competitions, saying their performances reflected India’s growing excellence in para-sports.
